causes.label: A fuse in your home may be blown or the circuit breaker tripped.
remedies: Replace fuse or reset circuit breaker.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 32: "A fuse in your home may be blown or the circuit breaker tripped."

causes.label: Power surge.
remedies: Unplug the microwave oven, then plug it back in.

causes.label: Plug not fully inserted into wall outlet
remedies: Make sure the 3-prong plug on the oven is fully inserted into wall outlet.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 32: "Plug not fully inserted into wall outlet"

causes.label: Door not securely closed.
remedies: Open the door and close securely.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 32: "Door not securely closed."

symptoms.symptom: Control panel lighted, yet oven will not start

causes.label: Door not securely closed.
remedies: Open the door and close securely.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 32: "Door not securely closed."

causes.label: START/PAUSE button not pressed after entering cooking selection.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 32: "START/PAUSE button not pressed after entering cooking selection."

causes.label: Another selection entered already in oven and CANCEL/ OFF button not pressed to cancel it.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 32: "Another selection entered already in oven and CANCEL/ OFF button not pressed to cancel it."

causes.label: Cooking time not entered after pressing COOK TIME
remedies: Make sure you have entered cooking time after pressing COOK TIME.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 32: "Cooking time not entered after pressing COOK TIME"

causes.label: CANCEL/OFF was pressed accidentally.
remedies: Reset cooking program and press START/PAUSE.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 32: "CANCEL/OFF was pressed accidentally."

causes.label: The control has been locked.
remedies: Press and hold CANCEL/OFF for about 3 seconds to unlock the control.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 32: "The control has been locked."

symptoms.symptom: Floor of the oven is warm even when the oven has not been used

causes.label: The cooktop light is located below the oven floor. When light is on, the heat it produces may make the oven floor get warm.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 32: "The cooktop light is located below the oven floor. When light is on, the heat it produces may make the oven floor get warm."

symptoms.symptom: You hear an unusual low-tone beep

causes.label: You have tried to change the power level when it is not allowed
remedies: Many of the oven’s features are preset and cannot be changed.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 32: "You have tried to change the power level when it is not allowed"

causes.label: The vent fan automatically turns on to protect the microwave if it senses too much heat rising from the cooktop below.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 32: "The vent fan automatically turns on to protect the microwave if it senses too much heat rising from the cooktop below."

causes.label: Power interruption may disrupt bluetooth connection
remedies: Try to reconnect by initiating the CHEF CONNECT process on the GE Range, then holding the CHEF CONNECT button for 3 seconds on the microwave.
This will restart the pairing process.
If this does not work, unplug unit or reset the circuit breaker to reset the control.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 32: "Power interruption may disrupt bluetooth connection"
